newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MIDWEST DIRECT HOGS SEEN OFF $0.50-$1-DEALERS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MIDWEST DIRECT HOGS SEEN OFF $0.50-$1-DEALERS.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower on outlooks for continued light packer demand and ample hog numbers, livestock dealers said.

"It's harder to turn them away than it is to buy them," one central Indiana hog dealer said. "We've been trying to talk everybody into waiting until next week to ship hogs, but its hard to do when the price is going down," he said.
Indiana/Ohio hogs were seen $1.00 lower, with a top of $56.50 to $57.00 at the plant, sources in that area said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top hog prices at the plant were expected $0.50-$1.00 lower at $57.00-$57.50, sources there said. Illinois hog prices at plants were expected $0.50-$1.00 lower, with tops ranging $56.50-$57.00.
Hog marketings this week were running slightly larger than expected as farmers catch up following light shipments last week, an Iowa buyer said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts on Tuesday totaled 115,000 head, above the estimate of 110,000, USDA said. Wednesday's estimate was 105,000 head, compared with an actual run of 102,000 a week ago.
